operations.evidence: Albanian, Romanian, Polish, Irish, and Indian nationals accounted for just under two-fifths of foreign national first receptions in 2025.
Counts by nationality must remain aggregate and cannot be used for person or parcel scoring.
There were 40,515 untried prison admissions in 2025, 3% more than in 2024.
Admissions are justice-system flows and not direct measures of local crime incidence.
There were 25,714 convicted unsentenced entries to custody in 2025, 1% more than in 2024.
The figure cannot be spatially joined to a parcel without event-level geography, which is absent.
There were 47,769 sentenced admissions to prison in 2025, a 2% increase from 2024.
Sentenced admissions do not identify local safety at an address.
Sentenced admissions for sentences under 12 months represented 44% of all sentenced admissions in 2025.
The share is a custody-flow composition measure only.
There were 47,742 immediate custodial admissions in 2025, 2% more than in 2024.
The total is national and cannot be treated as an area risk rate.
Immediate custodial admissions for public-order offences increased by 19% between 2024 and 2025.
The publication notes contextual policy and disorder effects; it does not support parcel attribution.
There were 45,432 recall admissions to custody in 2025, 28% more than in 2024.
Recall admissions reflect licence administration and policy as well as behaviour, so they are not a local crime proxy.
Recall admissions from determinate sentences of 12 months or more increased by 33% and represented 51% of all recall admissions.
Sentence-based recall flows cannot establish safety at a location.
There were 18,379 first receptions into custody between October and December 2025.
The quarterly national count is not exact-address evidence.
Quarterly first receptions comprised 12,771 remand, 5,502 sentenced, and 106 non-criminal first receptions.
The breakdown is institutional and cannot be assigned to parcels.
Total first receptions in October to December 2025 were 2% higher than in the same quarter of 2024.
The comparison does not identify local drivers.
Untried admissions were 9,699, convicted unsentenced admissions 6,277, and sentenced admissions 12,058 in the latest quarter.
These categories can overlap broader flows and are not parcel-level incident measures.
Recall admissions increased by 36% to 13,310 in October to December 2025 compared with the same quarter in 2024.
The increase is affected by recall policy and early-release schemes and cannot be used as a local crime score.
